sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong backward-looking quarter (EBIT of USD 1.3bn vs USD 177m a year ago), but full-year 2025 guidance for underlying EBITDA (USD 6-9bn), EBIT (USD 0-3bn), and free cash flow (at least negative USD 3bn) is all maintained unchanged. The container market volume growth outlook was revised down to -1% to 4% from 'around 4%' due to increased macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty. Management language is confident about operational progress but explicitly cautious on the forward outlook, citing 'considerable macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties' and a 'rapidly evolving trade policy landscape.' The net effect is a neutral score: the backward beat does not raise forward expectations, and the guidance is held flat with notable downside risks flagged.

summary.revenue: USD 13.3bn (USD 12.4bn in Q1 2024), an increase of 7.8% year-over-year.
summary.eps: Earnings per share of USD 74 (USD 11 in Q1 2024).
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 guidance maintained: underlying EBITDA USD 6-9bn, underlying EBIT USD 0-3bn, free cash flow at least negative USD 3.0bn. Global container market volume growth revised to -1% to 4% (from around 4%). Red Sea disruption expected to continue throughout the rest of the year.
summary.margin: EBITDA margin 20.3% (12.9% in Q1 2024). EBIT margin 9.4% (1.4% in Q1 2024).
key_risks: Increased macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty, particularly from US-China trade tensions and tariffs.
Global container market volume growth revised down to -1% to 4%.
Ocean segment experiencing a continuously declining rate environment since mid-2024.
Potential for a US recession if trade war escalates.
Red Sea disruption expected to last for the full year, impacting network costs.
Fulfilled by Maersk still delivering negative EBITDA.
Logistics & Services organic revenue growth (6.9%) below the 10% target.
Terminals ROIC expected to be negatively impacted by the Port Elizabeth concession extension.
key_opportunities: Logistics & Services EBIT margin improved to 4.1%, on track towards 6% target.
Gemini network launched successfully, offering greater flexibility and cost savings.
Terminals delivered strong results with ROIC of 14.5%, well above the 9% target.
Strong balance sheet with net cash of USD 5.2bn, allowing continued investment and shareholder returns.
Geographically diversified portfolio provides offsetting opportunities in non-US markets.
New solutions (Lead Logistics, bonded solutions, customs services) to support customers navigating tariffs.
